body:
A signal is modeled by S(x) = e^(3x) cos x. What is S'(x)?

Choices:
A. 3e^x cos(x)
B. -3e^(3x) sin(x)
C. e^(3x)(3cos(x) - sin(x))
D. e^(3x)(cos(x) - 3sin(x))

A concentration is modeled by C(x) = x^2 e^(-x). What is C'(x)?

Choices:
A. 2x e^(-x)
B. -2x e^(-x)
C. e^(-x)(2x - x^2)
D. e^(-x)(2x + x^2)

A damped voltage signal is modeled by D(x) = e^(−4x) cos x. What is D′(x)?

Choices:
A. e^(−4x)(4 cos x − sin x)
B. 4e^(−4x) sin x
C. −e^(−4x)(4 cos x + sin x)
D. e^(−4x)(sin x − 4 cos x)

Find d/dx [x² sin(3x)].

Choices:
A. 2x sin(3x) + x² cos(3x)
B. 2x sin(3x) + 3x² cos(3x)
C. 2x sin(3x) − 3x² cos(3x)
D. 6x cos(3x)

Find d/dx [x e^(x²)].

Choices:
A. 2x² e^(x²)
B. e^(x²)(1 + 2x²)
C. 2x e^(x²)
D. e^(x²)(1 + 2x)

A ramp's profile follows the curve y = √x. Which equation describes the line tangent to the profile at the point where x = 9?

Choices:
A. y = 3 + (x − 9)/3
B. y = 3 + (x − 9)/6
C. y = (x − 9)/6
D. y = 3 + 6(x − 9)

Find an equation of the tangent line to y = x·e^x at x = 1.

Choices:
A. y = e + e(x − 1)
B. y = 2e(x − 1)
C. y = e + 2e(x − 1)
D. y = e + (1 + e)(x − 1)

The hyperbola y = 1/x passes through the point with x-coordinate 2. Which equation describes the tangent line to the hyperbola there?

Choices:
A. y = 1/2 − (x − 2)/4
B. y = 2 − (x − 2)/4
C. y = 1/2 − (x − 2)/2
D. y = 1/2 + (x − 2)/4

The volume of a balloon is V(t) = 4t² cubic centimeters at time t seconds. Which of the following limits is equal to the instantaneous rate of change of V at t = 5?

Choices:
A. lim(h→0) [4(5+h)² − 4h²]/h
B. lim(h→0) [4(5+h)² − 100]/h
C. lim(h→0) [4(5+h)² − 100]/(5h)
D. lim(h→0) [4(5+h)² − 100]/5

If g(x) = x² cos x, find g′(x).

Choices:
A. 2x cos x − x² sin x
B. −2x sin x
C. −x² sin x
D. 2x cos x + x² sin x

The temperature of a metal part is defined by

T(t) = 2t + 1 for t < 1
T(1) = 5
T(t) = t^2 + 4 for t > 1

What is lim(t->1) T(t)?

Choices:
A. 5
B. The limit does not exist.
C. 3
D. 4

A signal is defined by

g(x) = sqrt(x + 13) - 1 for x < 3
g(3) = -4
g(x) = (x^2 - 3)/2 for x > 3

What is lim(x->3) g(x)?

Choices:
A. The limit does not exist.
B. -4
C. 4
D. 3

Two chemical amounts A(t) and B(t) both approach 0 as t approaches 7, so lim(t->7) A(t) = 0 and lim(t->7) B(t) = 0. Which of the following is true about lim(t->7) A(t)/B(t)?

Choices:
A. It is infinity, because the denominator approaches 0.
B. It equals 0, because the numerator approaches 0.
C. It does not exist, because B(t) approaches 0.
D. It cannot be determined from this information alone.

In each option, both f and g approach 0 as x approaches 2. For which pair does lim(x->2) f(x)/g(x) equal 3?

Choices:
A. f(x) = 6(x - 2)^2 and g(x) = 2(x - 2)^2
B. f(x) = 3(x - 2) and g(x) = (x - 2)^2
C. f(x) = x - 2 and g(x) = 3(x - 2)
D. f(x) = (x - 2)^3 and g(x) = 3(x - 2)^2

The reaction rate r(t), in millimoles per second, of an enzyme at time t minutes is modeled by r(t) = (2t^2 - 7t - 4)/(t - 4) for t != 4, and a lab instrument records r(4) = 3. Consider the following statements.

I. lim(t->4) r(t) exists.
II. r is continuous at t = 4.
III. r has a removable discontinuity at t = 4.

Which of the statements are true?

Choices:
A. II and III only
B. I only
C. I and III only
D. I and II only

A sensor's gain is modeled by g(x) = (sqrt(x + 7) - 3)/(x - 2) for x != 2, and the stored calibration value is g(2) = 1/6. Consider the following statements.

I. lim(x->2) g(x) exists.
II. g is continuous at x = 2.
III. g has a removable discontinuity at x = 2.

Which of the statements are true?

Choices:
A. I only
B. I and III only
C. I and II only
D. II and III only

A motor controller outputs the signed correction c(x) = (x^2 - 4x)/|x - 4| for x != 4, where x is the commanded position in centimeters. Which of the following is true about lim(x->4) c(x)?

Choices:
A. The limit is 0.
B. The limit is 4.
C. The limit does not exist because the one-sided limits are -4 and 4.
D. The limit is -4.

In a circuit model, a polarity readout is p(v) = |2v + 6|/(v + 3) for v != -3, where v is a voltage in volts. Which of the following is true about lim(v->-3) p(v)?

Choices:
A. The limit is 2.
B. The limit is -2.
C. The limit does not exist because p is unbounded near v = -3.
D. The limit does not exist because the one-sided limits are -2 and 2.

A firm's profit swing at output level q (in thousands of units) is modeled by s(q) = |q^2 - 25|/(q - 5) for q != 5. Which of the following is true about lim(q->5) s(q)?

Choices:
A. The limit is -10.
B. The limit does not exist because the one-sided limits are -10 and 10.
C. The limit is 10.
D. The limit is 0.

An acoustics student proposes four formulas for the intensity I(d) of a sound source at distance d meters. Which formula becomes unbounded, that is, has an infinite discontinuity, at d = 2?

Choices:
A. I(d) = 3/(e^(d - 2) - 1)
B. I(d) = (d^3 - 8)/(d - 2)
C. I(d) = 4 for d < 2 and I(d) = 9 - d for d >= 2
D. I(d) = (d - 2)/(d^2 + 1)

A hockey puck is moved between two points on a rough horizontal surface, once along a straight line and once along a longer curved path. Kinetic friction acts on the puck the whole time. Which statement about the work done on the puck by friction is correct?

Choices:
A. The work is the same on both paths, because the endpoints are the same.
B. The work is zero on both paths, because the surface is horizontal.
C. The work is larger in magnitude along the longer curved path.
D. The work is positive on both paths, because the friction force is pushing along the surface.

A ball is thrown straight up, rises, and falls back to the height of the hand that threw it. Air resistance is not negligible. Which statement describes the net work done on the ball over the whole trip?

Choices:
A. Gravity does negative net work, and air resistance does zero net work.
B. Gravity does zero net work, and air resistance does negative net work.
C. Both gravity and air resistance do zero net work, because the ball returns to its starting height.
D. Both gravity and air resistance do negative net work, because both oppose the upward motion.

A crate is moved from the bottom of a rough ramp to a platform at the top by two different routes: a short straight slide and a long, winding slide. Both start and end at the same two points. Which statement is correct?

Choices:
A. The work done by gravity is the same for both routes, but the work done by friction is not.
B. The work done by gravity and the work done by friction are both the same for both routes.
C. The work done by friction is the same for both routes, but the work done by gravity is not.
D. The work done by gravity and the work done by friction both differ between the routes.

A rotating gate turns through an angle of 210°. What is this angle in radians?

Choices:
A. 6π/7
B. 7π/6
C. 7π/12
D. 7π/3

A turntable rotates through 135°. Which is the equivalent angle measure in radians?

Choices:
A. 4π/3
B. 135π
C. 3π/8
D. 3π/4

A clockwise rotation of 120° is represented by the angle −120°. What is −120° in radians?

Choices:
A. 2π/3
B. −π/3
C. −2π/3
D. −3π/2

No calculator is permitted.

For equally spaced inputs x=0, 1, 2, 3, 4, a table gives y=3, 4, 7, 12, 19. Which model type is most appropriate, and why?

Choices:
A. Cubic, because the first differences are not constant
B. Linear, because the first differences (1, 3, 5, 7) increase by a steady amount
C. Exponential, because the outputs increase by a larger amount each step
D. Quadratic, because the second differences are constant (all equal to 2)

No calculator is permitted.

Equally spaced inputs x=0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 produce the outputs 0, −1, 4, 21, 56, 115. Which kind of function best fits these values?

Choices:
A. A quartic model; the third differences are not zero
B. A cubic model; the third differences are all 6
C. A quadratic model; the second differences 6, 12, 18, 24 grow steadily
D. An exponential model; the first differences keep growing

No calculator is permitted.

A ball's height h (in feet) is recorded every half second: for t=0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 seconds, h=2, 8, 12, 14, 14. Which model type is most appropriate for h as a function of t?

Choices:
A. Cubic, with a negative leading coefficient
B. Quadratic, with a positive leading coefficient
C. Quadratic, with a negative leading coefficient
D. Linear, with a positive slope

Calculator use is permitted.

For g(x)=2x³−5x, what is the average rate of change from x=0.8 to x=2.3, to the nearest tenth?

Choices:
A. 15.8
B. 10.5
C. 23.7
D. −10.5

Calculator use is permitted.

For h(x)=x⁴−3x³+x, what is the average rate of change from x=1.4 to x=3.1, to the nearest tenth?

Choices:
A. 2.9
B. 5.3
C. −5.3
D. 9.1

Calculator use is permitted.

A drone's height (in meters) t seconds after launch is d(t)=0.2t⁴−1.5t²+3t. What is the average rate of change of its height from t=0.5 to t=2.5, in meters per second, to the nearest tenth?

Choices:
A. −2.4
B. 3.5
C. 2.4
D. 4.8

Calculator use is permitted.

For x=0, 1, 2, 3, 4, a measured quantity has values 5.0, 8.1, 10.9, 14.0, 17.1. Which claim is best supported?

Choices:
A. An exponential model, because every ratio of successive values is greater than 1
B. A linear model, because the first differences are all close to 3
C. A quadratic model, because the second differences are exactly constant
D. No model, because the first differences are not all identical

Calculator use is permitted.

For x=0, 1, 2, 3, 4, a quantity has values 80, 60.4, 45.1, 34.2, 25.6. Which claim is best supported?

Choices:
A. A quadratic model, because the second differences are exactly constant
B. An exponential decay model, because successive ratios are near 0.75
C. A linear model, because a linear regression has r² greater than 0.95
D. An exponential growth model, because the outputs are multiplied by about 1.33 each step

Calculator use is permitted.

A lab technician records a quantity at the whole-number inputs x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and obtains 2, 5, 10, 17, 26. Based on these data, which claim is best supported?

Choices:
A. A quadratic model, because the second differences are constant
B. An exponential model, because every ratio of successive values is greater than 1
C. No model, because the first differences are not constant
D. A linear model, because the average rate of change over [0, 4] is 6

Calculator use is permitted.

A logarithmic regression is y=3.2+4.1ln(x). What x gives y=15, to the nearest tenth?

Choices:
A. 17.8
B. 755.2
C. 38.8
D. 84.7

Calculator use is permitted.

A population model is P(t)=12e^(0.07t), where t is in years. At what time t is P(t)=50, to the nearest tenth?

Choices:
A. 8.9
B. 55.9
C. 52.0
D. 20.4

Calculator use is permitted.

A model is y=7.5−2.4ln(x). What x gives y=3, to the nearest tenth?

Choices:
A. 6.5
B. 79.4
C. 0.2
D. 3.5
